summary: Terra is a web app that lets anyone see how Romania’s climate is changing, using NASA open data only. You pick a town, county or map area, a period, and one of 354 monthly variables measured by NASA missions or produced by NASA models (from Giovanni and NASA POWER). Terra draws the time series and answers the challenge’s four questions: what is changing, where, how much, and whether the change is significant. It reports the rate per decade, its 95% range and two significance tests, in plain words. A map shows the trend at all 42 county seats, and a heat-map view draws real MODIS satellite observations at 500 m to 1 km, keeping only pixels NASA flags as good. You can also just ask a question in plain English. Terra matters because the data are free, but reading them is hard: it turns them into answers a teacher, journalist or town hall can check in seconds.
details:
Terra shows how Romania’s climate is changing, from NASA open data only. Pick a place, a period and one of 354 variables; it draws the time series, gives the rate of change per decade and tests whether it is significant. A map shows the trend at all 42 county seats, and a heat-map view shows MODIS satellite observations. You can also just ask a question in plain English.

For example, teachers, journalists and town halls can check a climate claim for their own town in seconds, in plain words.

Tools: Python, FastAPI, SciPy, SQLite, JavaScript, Leaflet, Docker; NASA Giovanni, POWER and AppEEARS; Anthropic Claude API for API Key for chatbot.

One question drives the whole tool, and statistics are translated into plain words.

Scientific validity (two tests, 95% range), real data only, and a language model that never computes the numbers.
